text:
Situation: Ketamine hydrochloride is listed by FDA as To Be Discontinued with an initial posting date of 2018-02-16. Corvale East holds 39 vials of the 50 mg/mL, 10 mL presentation at 7.2 vials per day, providing 5.4 days on hand. Corvale General holds 126 vials of the same presentation at 7.7 vials per day, providing 16.4 days on hand. Other presentations at Corvale East, Corvale General, and Corvale Lakeside have between 7.2 and 25 days on hand.

Why (FDA record): FDA lists ketamine hydrochloride as To Be Discontinued since 2018-02-16. A registered plant on our labels, Hospira, Inc. (FEI 1925262), received an OAI classification from inspection 976095 ending 2016-06-08, which was 618 days before the shortage posting. The same plant later received a Warning Letter on 2017-02-14 (367 days before posting) and another OAI classification from inspection 1064827 ending 2018-08-15 (180 days after posting).

Our position: We have sufficient inventory at Corvale General to support internal transfers that will extend days on hand at Corvale East and Corvale Lakeside while maintaining at least two weeks of supply at Corvale General. Purchasing from alternative manufacturers not on the FDA shortage list is a viable secondary strategy.

Recommended actions:
1. Transfer 18 vials of 50 mg/mL, 10 mL from Corvale General to Corvale East — requires pharmacy director approval and a controlled-substance transfer record (Schedule III-V).
2. Transfer 15 vials of 100 mg/mL, 5 mL from Corvale General to Corvale Lakeside — requires pharmacy director approval and a controlled-substance transfer record (Schedule III-V).
3. Transfer 81 vials of 100 mg/mL, 5 mL from Corvale General to Corvale East — requires pharmacy director approval and a controlled-substance transfer record (Schedule III-V).
4. Purchase from Fresenius Kabi USA, LLC — requires buyer approval.
5. Purchase from Par Health USA, LLC — requires buyer approval.

Not recommended: No clinical dosing changes or formulary substitutions at this time; those decisions remain with treating clinicians and the committee.
